title: Weber-overnight four-member alternating ring: preregistered instrument runs (machine record)
status: complete: preregistration, known cases (11/11 pass), WR-0 (4 radii x 2 tolerances), rates (18 cases x 2), events (18 cases x 2), WR-8 (2) recorded; readable account written into the ring file section 10
worker: henri-poincare lens (subject lane), weber-overnight ring instrument runs
law: equation-variants/manuscript.md Section 9; lambda_W=-1/2, mu_W=1, K=c_f=1; instantaneous support; unit integration weights; no clamp, delay or softening
grade: measured by the subject instrument (double-precision GBS with event location); not an enclosure. Same-lane caveat: the predictions compared against come from the ring derivation written in this lane; the instrument and the derivation share no code, but the blind independent check is a separate lane.

preregistration.geometry: centre at rest; ring in the xy plane; member j at rho (cos(j pi/2), sin(j pi/2), 0); polarity q_j = (-1)^j, member 0 (index 0, the file's member 1) at (rho,0,0) with +; counterclockwise rotation at Omega = sqrt((2 sqrt2 - 1)/(4 rho^3)); member speed Omega rho, set exactly to 1 at x_* when it rounds to 1 within 8e-16

events.turning: not recorded (ring separations are stationary to round-off on the balanced state and would generate round-off turning points at every step); separation extremes are taken from the recorded states instead

preregistration.speedRecordingException: WR-0 at x_* has every member exactly at c_f; a round-off crossing would be reported at every step, so speed recording is off for that one case and the member speed range is reported from the states instead

WR-0.record: survival, radius drift, invariant drift, smallest |det M|, member speed and label

WR-1..WR-7.durations: eps=1e-6: 3 rotation periods or first stopping event (fit window only); eps=1e-3: first stopping event or 20 periods; every run also stops at 40000 accepted steps, recorded as max-steps (a cost stop, not an event)
WR-1..WR-7.note: relative to rho; position displacement only (no velocity added), so each run excites a mixture within its sector and the fit uses the full sector model; WR-4b adds a velocity eps*rho*Omega*(1,0,0) to every member instead
WR-1..WR-7.fit: variable-projection least squares of the sector amplitude on the early window (amplitude below 100 eps rho and t below 3 periods), nonlinear parameters found by grid search then Nelder-Mead; k=1 sublattice uses |S|^2 = P e^{2 gamma t} + Q + R e^{-2 gamma t}; k=2 uses four roots +-sqrt(s_1), +-sqrt(s_2); oscillatory sectors use offset + cos/sin
WR-1..WR-7.events: first event (kind, members, time), minimum pair separation history, pairing diagnosis on the final window

WR-8.perturbation: breathing (radial) displacement 1e-2 rho, no velocity change
WR-8.record: reduced breathing energy E_red of ring Section 6 (6.3) drift; turning points of rho against the roots of (6.3); first time any symmetry-breaking sector amplitude exceeds 1e-8 rho

preregistration.pairingRule: on the final window (last 10% of states, at least 20): the matching with the smallest sum of pair separations must be the same at every state, both pairs opposite polarity, max pair separation <= 0.25 of the minimum pair-centre distance, and the pair-centre distance larger at the end of the window than at its start

familyRadiusCheck.note: the 1e-2 radial displacement at fixed velocity moves the family radius to rho0 = ell^2/(4(2 sqrt2-1)K); the fitted frequency is compared with (5.2) evaluated at rho0

anomalies: WR-1 breathing (position-only displacement) misses the 1e-6 rate target at 2.1e-5 relative: the start shifts the family radius by 2 eps and the rotation phase drifts linearly (Jordan block); the radial projection carries the second-order term -rho dphi^2/2 of that drift, absent from the fitted model (fit residual 1.1e-4 against <=1e-10 elsewhere). WR-5 recovers the same frequency to 5e-9.

Step cap: 40000 accepted steps for WR-1, WR-2, WR-3 at x=1.7, eps=1e-3 (prereg runs) and 15000 for every later run, lowered after the sandbox per-call time limit (about 120 s) was discovered; max-steps terminations are cost stops. Tight binaries with members above c_f cross the speed boundary every orbit and each crossing is located by re-stepping, which dominates the cost.

x=0.8, x_*, x=0.3: every run ends in step-underflow (or the cap) with one like-polarity pair ((0,2) or (1,3)) at separation 3e-5 (rtol 1e-12) to 7e-6 (rtol 1e-10) and member speeds 4e4 to 3e5 c_f, still closing; the contact threshold 1e-6 and the obstruction thresholds were never reached (|det M| >= 7.9 at x=0.8). Interpretation as a finite-time singularity is graded inferred.

x=0.8 eps=1e-6: the 100 eps windows of the k=1 and elliptic fits are already nonlinear (residual 1e-4) because the fast root 3.43 reaches 100 eps within 1.3 time units; the 10 eps windows carry the comparison.

Sublattice phase rate Omega/m_s recovered only to 0.75 percent (100 eps window) because the phase of the two-root mixture settles to the growing root value only after several e-foldings; weak check only.
H drift of the instrument summaries reaches 1e-5 to 1e-4 in the tight-binary phase of the x=1.7 runs; the early windows used for the fits have drift below 1e-10.
Background processes do not survive between sandbox tool calls; the runner was made resumable (reload results, skip recorded cases) and invoked repeatedly; resumedUTC lists the invocations.
